summary: Correct the subject person in the translation

summary: Restore the resentment expressed by leba fayəš-wa m-u=abro
before: Her heart had been filled with grief because of her son.
after: She had been angry with her son.
rationale: The Turoyo construction leba fayəš-wa m-u=abro illustrates the entry’s sense 2, “übelnehmen, böse sein auf (mene)”. It describes her resentment toward her son, not grief about him. The edition confirms “Sie war ja auch ihrem Sohne gram”; the following clause explains his refusal to work.

summary: 78/224 is remaining time before recovery, not resentment (sense 2).

summary: Routine counts supplied with this batch: 960 I/Preterit Intransitive/1; 363 I/Infectum/1; 110 I/Preterit Intransitive/3; 58 I/Preterit Intransitive/4; 51 I/Imperativ/1; 45 I/Infectum-wa/1; 25 I/Preterit-wa/1; 2 I/Infinitiv/1; 1 I/Preterit/4; 1 I/Preterit-wa/2. These are aggregate input evidence, not additional individual decisions.

Aspect: inflected feminine/plural Preterit Intransitive and first-person Infectum support continuation in sense 3. Default fayəš also occurs with non-masculine participants; agreement and auxiliary invariance must be investigated separately. Negative nominal remainder (no thieves, no community) remains sense 1; negative scope over a lexical action belongs to sense 4. JTM 4.4/17 has rhetorical negative force.

Experiencer sense 2: lebo is the grammatical subject, the affected person is its possessor, and men- marks the target/stimulus (JTM 1.3/45, PrS 18/3). Remaining-time 78/224 lacks that frame and is moved to sense 1.

Valency: l-suffixes often mark an affected possessor/beneficiary of a remainder, not an agent. Coordinated and plural referents sometimes occur with default singular forms. The existing distinction between Preterit and Preterit Intransitive is retained; uncertain contractions are not silently normalized.

Dialect: p/f variation (kopayši, Payišowa), contracted fāš/fōš, and Imperativ fəš are preserved as supplied. Substantivized fayoše 'settlers' is filed as Part act. consistently with this glossary's agent-noun convention (compare ḥlw ḥalawto and lbk laboko), while its productivity versus lexicalization remains a question.
Collocation lookup in inputs returned no match for ḥaṣra, rišux basimo, b riš, qorqor, or fayoš. rfy III already quotes 36/102; the new fyš collocation cross-files that use without modifying rfy.

PrS reference differences may reflect different citation systems: retain the inherited prs 13/13, 27/3, 42/7 references, and raise crosswalk questions. The supplied darwīš verse is compatible with continuing service under revised sense 3, so no forced move to sense 1 is made.

Batch 2 continues batch 1 cumulatively. Sense 5 is independently confirmed by 77/138; 78/224 confirms the earlier move of the duration example from resentment to sense 1. No earlier numbering or decisions are reversed.

Continuation: 74/24 kfayši məǧġoli and 75/242 fayiši kogəḥki support inflected auxiliary agreement; 63/109 kofaš ... kokoleno establishes negative sense 4 in Infectum. Distinguish these from nominal remaining and abstract resultant status.

fašlux 62/65–69 is assigned to Preterit consistently with fašlux 60/90–93 in batch 1; this corrects the reader's box, not an inherited example. The morphological comparison remains an editor question.
Experiencer sense 2 is confirmed by lebe/lebayye plus reciprocal men- at 95/34 and 95/163; contracted foš at 65/220 retains the heart subject, so it is not an Imperativ.

The supplied 63/230 Fayišo with a coordinated first-person subject and 107/150 fayšono in a hypothetical future cannot be normalized from translation tense alone. They remain questions. No quotation is taken from a reader context that expands beyond the supplied verse.

Final synthesis groups responsibility at 83/41 with dependence/up-to sense 5: the ʕal-person determines or bears the undertaking. The broader gloss is supported by batch 2 and retains all earlier numbering; no separate 5b is introduced.

All 125 supplied occurrence records were reviewed; repeated forms in one verse retain separate ordered decisions. No routine counts are supplied. Jan includes dialogue and repairs as well as literary discussion; register differences are not reducible to modern written prose alone.

Nominal negative remainder is I.1: ḥarb (Jan 1.8/156), churches (Jan 2.10/2471), bride-price (Jan 4.II/969–970). Negative scope over a lexical action is I.4: laybi fayəš mḥamenolxu (Jan 1.22/1121), lə kuḏaʕno fayəš (Jan 1.36/1532). This preserves the round 1 distinction.
Experiencer I.2 appears as fyošo d lebo alongside ġəbən and mḥoyo (Jan 1.39/1719); the nominal lebo frame does not establish a new meaning or a finite direct-object construction.

Positive and negative suffix-shaped fəšle, fəšlan, fəšše recur in several speakers and contexts. The existing Preterit box is used provisionally; these do not by themselves establish an agent or transitive valency. qaṭəl fayišina and fəšlan contrast within Jan 2.3/364. -wo-le/-wo-la and doubled fəšlewole are retained verbatim in evidence notes rather than normalized.

Apparent default agreement occurs with plural maḥoye/sayome at Jan 3.43/1216 and feminine ḥḏo at Jan 1.21/1049; compare an immediate fayšiwa → fayšowa repair at Jan 3.49/1376. Do not treat a repair as a productive agreement paradigm.

Round 1 already supplies five Imperativ/1 and five Infectum-wa/1 examples. Jan’s repeated stay commands and routine preserved-bin contexts are therefore not added as thin-cell material. Part act. fayoše in Jan 2.4/556 supports the existing round 1 proposal; uncertain fayišo in Jan 4.II/1002 cannot establish a further form.

Existing immediate-death b-i=dukṯo and round 1 riš- basimo blessing recur in Jan 1.21/963–965, Jan 2.29/4701–4703 and Jan 3.1/4; no duplicate idioms are proposed. Search raġlo returned other roots but no fyš expression; search b boli returned no result.

Correct began → begann
rationale: The German past tense of beginnen is begann. The edition at 21/55 has “begann er sich zu grämen”.

summary: Correct began → begann
rationale: The German past tense of beginnen is spelled begann, with final nn.

summary: Capitalize the noun Tropfen
rationale: Tropfen is a noun here and must be capitalized. The edition at 29/18 also has “einen Tropfen Milch”.

summary: Correct the reversed words in nicht wahr?
rationale: The German tag question is “nicht wahr?”. The edition renders latyo hawxa with “nicht wahr?” at JL 7.7/4.

summary: Lowercase the verb stach
rationale: Stach is a finite verb inside the clause “wenn der einen Menschen stach”; the edition at JL 7.7/6 also has lowercase stach.

summary: Separate zu hören after ohne etwas
rationale: Here etwas is the object of hören: “without hearing anything”. The infinitive is zu hören. The joined verb zuhören means “listen” and does not take etwas as a direct object.

summary: Remaining covers preserved food and stores, surviving shrines and communities, abstract qualities, deceased persons/remains, and property left to a possessor. These participant changes do not justify separate senses.

Remaining in a school grade, remaining over a besieged town, and remaining motionless in a magical tableau specialize the state/location in context. No independent repeat-a-grade, besiege, or freeze lexical sense is established.
Measured time may be the remaining interval or frame a maintained situation. Do not infer an independent pass/elapse sense solely from German 'Nach Verlauf' or 'es dauerte'.
Part act. fayoše 'settlers' names people by their staying/settling; agent-noun filing follows the glossary convention, without a new finite lexical sense.
Nominal negative remainder can denote no work left to someone or no further beatings. It does not by itself establish sense 4, whose diagnostic is negative scope over a following action.

Jan independently supports round 1 continuation with invariant/postposed fayəš, finite kfoyəš and suffix-shaped fəšle/fəšwole; morphological identity of the latter remains open.
Language/culture survival, geographical location, remembered content, abstract freedom and inherited property extend existing remaining/state meaning; do not create senses for each participant class.
